title: Unchecked error return in Go

finding.title: unchecked error
finding.summary: The error return from os.WriteFile is discarded, so disk-full, permission, and invalid-path failures are silently swallowed and callers assume the config was saved.

title: Hardcoded database credentials in Go

finding.title: hardcoded secret
finding.summary: Production database username, password, and host are committed in plaintext as package-level constants, exposing credentials to anyone with repository access.

title: Nil-pointer dereference on missing map value in Go

finding.title: nil dereference
finding.summary: FindUser dereferences u.Email without checking that the map lookup returned a non-nil pointer, so a missing id causes a nil pointer dereference and a process crash.

title: Data race on a shared Go map

finding.title: Concurrent map access is not synchronized
finding.summary: Multiple goroutines read and write the same map without a mutex or another synchronization boundary.

title: SQL injection via fmt.Sprintf in Go

finding.title: sql injection
finding.summary: User-supplied email is interpolated into the SQL query via fmt.Sprintf instead of parameterized placeholders, allowing injection of arbitrary SQL.

title: Predictable PRNG for security tokens in Java

finding.title: insecure random
finding.summary: Reset tokens are generated with java.util.Random, a predictable PRNG whose seed is recoverable from observed outputs, allowing token forgery. SecureRandom should be used instead.

title: Arbitrary code execution via eval() in JavaScript

finding.title: code injection
finding.summary: Caller-supplied expression is passed directly to eval(), turning any user-controlled value into executing JavaScript and enabling arbitrary code execution.

title: Open redirect via unvalidated URL in Express

finding.title: open redirect
finding.summary: The next query parameter is passed directly to res.redirect without an allowlist or same-origin check, enabling phishing redirects off the trusted domain.

title: Bare except swallows all errors in Python

finding.title: swallowed error
finding.summary: A bare except catches BaseException (including KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit), hides JSON parse failures, and silently returns an empty dict so callers never learn the config failed to parse.

title: Command injection via subprocess shell=True in Python

finding.title: command injection
finding.summary: subprocess.run is called with shell=True and a string command containing user-controlled host, allowing shell metacharacters to inject arbitrary commands.

title: Hardcoded cloud API credentials in Python

finding.title: hardcoded secret
finding.summary: A live AWS access key id and secret access key are hardcoded in source. Anyone with repository access can extract and abuse these credentials.

title: Insecure pickle deserialization in Python

finding.title: insecure deserialization
finding.summary: pickle.loads is called on a user-supplied base64 blob. pickle can execute arbitrary code during deserialization, so untrusted input lets an attacker run any payload on the server.

title: Path traversal in a Python file handler

finding.title: Untrusted path escapes the intended directory
finding.summary: The requested filename is joined to the storage root without canonical containment validation.

title: SQL injection via f-string in Python

finding.title: sql injection
finding.summary: User-supplied name is interpolated into the SQL query via an f-string, allowing injection of arbitrary SQL such as a UNION SELECT to exfiltrate other tables.

title: Server-side request forgery in Python

finding.title: ssrf
finding.summary: The server fetches a user-supplied URL with no scheme, host, or private-range restrictions, allowing requests to cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254) to steal credentials or to internal services for pivoting.

title: Weak password hashing with MD5 in Python

finding.title: weak crypto
finding.summary: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5, which is cryptographically broken and trivially reversed with rainbow tables; identical passwords produce identical hashes.

title: Unbounded zip extraction (zip bomb) in Python

finding.title: resource exhaustion
finding.summary: extractall is called without checking uncompressed sizes or compression ratios, so a small zip bomb can decompress to petabytes and exhaust disk and memory.

title: Unchecked integer arithmetic in Rust

finding.title: integer overflow
finding.summary: credit uses += on u64 without checked/saturating arithmetic; in release builds an overflowing credit wraps the balance silently, enabling balance manipulation.

title: Unreachable code after unconditional return

finding.title: dead code
finding.summary: The if (score >= 70) branch and final return are unreachable because an unconditional return at line 8 always exits the function first.

title: Hardcoded database password in TypeScript

finding.title: hardcoded secret
finding.summary: The production database password is committed in plaintext inside the source file, exposing credentials to anyone with repository access.

title: Insecure session cookie attributes in TypeScript

finding.title: insecure cookie
finding.summary: The session cookie is set without Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite attributes, so it is transmitted over HTTP, readable by JavaScript/XSS, and vulnerable to CSRF.

title: Missing await on async operation in TypeScript

finding.title: missing await
finding.summary: deleteSession returns a promise but is not awaited, so a rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection and logout resolves before the session is actually deleted, leaving stale sessions.

title: Prototype pollution via recursive merge in TypeScript

finding.title: prototype pollution
finding.summary: The recursive merge walks user-supplied keys without blocking __proto__/constructor/prototype, so a payload like {"__proto__": {"admin": true}} pollutes Object.prototype and escalates privileges across the application.

title: Catastrophic backtracking regex (ReDoS) in TypeScript

finding.title: regex dos
finding.summary: The regex uses a nested + quantifier ((...+)+) causing exponential backtracking on non-matching inputs; a long crafted string hangs the event loop and denies service to all other requests.

title: SQL injection in a TypeScript lookup

finding.title: User input is interpolated into an executed SQL query
finding.summary: The lookup builds SQL with user-controlled email input instead of a parameterized query.

title: Type-safety bypass via `as any` in TypeScript

finding.title: type confusion
finding.summary: The payload is cast through `as any` to Order, bypassing the compiler so a Refund-shaped object is treated as an Order; at runtime items is undefined and the .length access throws or silently corrupts downstream totals.

title: Reflected XSS via dangerouslySetInnerHTML in React

finding.title: xss
finding.summary: User-supplied comment body is rendered as raw HTML via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without any sanitization, enabling stored/reflected XSS.
